It differs from its parent [Depth to 3D Points Conversion](7929-depth-to-3d-points-conversion.md) by applying explicit downsampling factors and stride ratios to control point density [S1, unofficial], and from its sibling [Point Cloud Generation and Refinement](8042-point-cloud-generation-and-refinement.md) by relying on direct geometric backprojection rather than implicit field refinement [S2].

The claim states that the method differs from [S1] by applying explicit downsampling factors and stride ratios to control point density. Source [S1] explicitly mentions 'downsampling images by a factor ds' and 'uniformly subsampling valid depth points with stride ratio' to control point density. The claim also states it differs from [S2] by relying on direct geometric backprojection rather than implicit field refinement. Source [S2] describes its method as recovering explicit geometry from implicit fields by rendering optimized radiance fields (implicit) to RGBD maps and then backprojecting. Thus, [S2] relies on implicit field refinement (rendering from implicit fields) to generate the point cloud, whereas the claim implies the subject method uses direct backprojection (as seen in S1's description of backprojecting RGB-D observations directly). The evidence supports the distinction described.
